note: Capital work-in-progress (CWIP) and intangible assets under development (IAUD), park by park (the CWIP sheet of the signed workbook). Zoho Books keeps two ledger accounts for them, Capital Work in Progress and Intangible Asset Under Development; neither has a park column. Zoho's FY26 books were rebuilt at the year end, so almost all of the money arrived through clean-up journals dated 31-Mar-2026 (JN-Clean-n, 'Transfering ledger balance from old to new ledger') that empty an OLD ledger account into the new one - and the old account's NAME says the park ('Land Lease Dechu', 'Connectivity Charges Kolayat NPD', 'Civil Work Napasar'). The auditors' own journals (SJ-1121 ... SJ-1130, 289) say the park in their text. Bills carry a project ('NPD - Panchu - TL') and a narration. So every line of the two ledgers is given a park by the WORDS in its journal's notes and old-ledger name, or in the bill's project / narration / location. A line that names no park (or two) is allocated by an entry of `allocate` below, and said so on the tab. The total of each park (both accounts together, as booked) is what the CWIP tab compares with the sum of its three columns. The split of a park between the three columns (pure services, boundary wall and road, transmission line and MCR) is the auditors' own classification: Zoho only has the two accounts, and one journal (SJ-1130, 'adjustment made to boundary wall & road') moves Rs 12,01,37,795 from CWIP to IAUD without saying park by park where it comes from. That journal is shown separately and left out of the parks (it nets to nil).
